conn_runs_exchange.detail: Three distinct synthetic message index entries: Alice has one, Bob has two, leaf size is 1 and wire chunks hold one ID. Kernel proofs construct the actual Conn.start and alternating onRbsr execution, a fingerprint-to-IDs hop forced by unequal counts, terminal batch, initial active epochs, sorted and uniquely named items, empty initial asks, and sufficient ask capacity at every step. A native production-SHA check enumerates all filtered subsets and their actual Merkle inputs; sound_of_check lifts this finite collision check to every possible range, with no universal SHA axiom or substituted hash. The certificate applies conn_runs_exchange, which proves finite claim termination and actual wire have/want coverage of exchange's set difference. The consequence is instantiated separately for all three missing IDs; a nonempty later pending ask is traced to its earlier actual want. Negative controls reject a constant hash and show zero ask capacity suppresses the want. The two ends' indices are fixed, so this is the fixed-index case of live_round_complete; whole Node/TCP scheduling, data transport, request queue admission, and validation remain separate composition obligations. No collected real-user messages are claimed.

RoundRun.terminates.detail: The same actual two-party execution: every index the run reads is one of the two fixtures, so their union bounds it; RoundRun.terminates ends the round within 8 batches, with the run and its currency derived from the actual handlers.
